relevance_note: Single case report of an identifiable patient with LAD-1 and ITGB2 compound heterozygosity: 'We report a case of a 24-year-old female patient with LAD-1'.
method_note: Read the paper by hand; a Python script only assembled the JSON. No tables in the paper. Scope: the patient plus both parents, who are described as tested in relation to her ('present in both of the patient's parents'); parents' sex not stated, so labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'. Variants: the paper prints no variant description ('2 novel mutations'), so the patient has two ITGB2 rows with variant_original_string 'not reported'; the gene is named only in the general Discussion sentence on LAD-1, and is given as the span with the patient's sentence. Reference [5]'s title mentions 'A novel 3′ splice-site mutation and a novel gross deletion', but the text does not tie these classes to the patient's variants explicitly, so variant_type is 'not reported'. Inheritance: 'which were present in both of the patient's parents' does not say which parent carries which variant (read literally it could mean both variants in both parents, which is unclear for a compound heterozygote), so 'inherited unspecified parent' for each of the patient's variants; each parent gets one variant row with string, zygosity and inheritance 'not reported'. Prior report: cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true rests on 'which we had previously reported' (the mutations, with citation ^5); the wording is about the mutations rather than the patient explicitly. Age at onset left 'not reported': the earliest event is a soft tissue infection 'at the age of 3', but the paper does not call it onset; first presentation was at 6. Age at diagnosis not stated. 'Abdominal ultrasound and chest radiography did not result in any pathologic findings' recorded as written (excluded), excluding nothing more specific (D-27). 'Inflamed ulcer'/'chronic wound' not described as necrotic, so the checklist item 'necrotic skin ulcers or pyoderma gangrenosum-like lesions' is not reported. Discussion statements about LAD-1 patients in general (tooth loss, mortality) were not applied to the patient. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: No allogeneic HSCT (no matching donor); topical granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor for the wound; parenteral antibiotics and intravenous immunoglobulins (2 g/kg) for recurrent wounds; surgical intervention for facial soft tissue infection at age 3; vaccinations against viral infections and skin disinfection as surveillance
span: No matching bone marrow donor was available; we thus proceeded without allogeneic HSCT
The wound was treated with topical granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, which induced healing over 8 weeks.
Therapy included parenteral antibiotics (depending on skin cultures) and intravenous immunoglobulins (2 g/kg body weight), resulting in prompt wound healing.
severe facial soft tissue infection and consecutive surgical intervention at the age of 3
vaccinations against viral infections to prevent bacterial superinfections, genetic counseling, intensive skin disinfection before blood sampling
